ACADEMIC REGULATIONS & CURRICULUM GUIDELINES (B.TECH)
=====================================================

Section 1: General Academic Structure and Credits
1.1 Total Credits Required for Graduation
Every student admitted to the four-year Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) degree program shall pursue a full-time course of study for eight semesters. The total number of credits required for the award of the B.Tech degree is strictly 160 credits. For students admitted under the Lateral Entry Scheme into the third semester (second year), the total number of credits required for graduation is 120 credits.

Section 2: Attendance Requirements and Condonation Rules
2.1 Minimum Attendance Requirement
A student shall be eligible to appear for the semester end examinations only if the student acquires a minimum of 75% attendance in aggregate of all subjects registered in that semester. Attendance is computed from the date of commencement of instruction up to the last instructional day.

Section 4: Maximum Duration and Promotion Regulations
4.1 Time Limit for Degree Completion
A student must complete all requirements for the B.Tech degree within a maximum span of 8 academic years (N + 4 years from the date of initial enrollment). A lateral entry student must complete the degree within 6 academic years. Failure to meet all academic requirements within this window leads to automatic forfeiture of student registration.

TRAINING & PLACEMENT GUIDELINES, CORPORATE POLICIES AND ELIGIBILITY
===================================================================

Section 1: Placement Eligibility Criteria
1.1 Standard Academic Cutoffs for Campus Recruitment
Students seeking placement assistance through the Training and Placement Cell (T&P Cell) must satisfy the prescribed academic and attendance thresholds. Registration with the T&P portal is mandatory by the 6th semester.

placement_guidelines_p1_c1_cfe88c953018.text:

Key Provisions:
  * Minimum CGPA: A cumulative grade point average of 6.5 (or 60% aggregate marks) with no standing/active backlogs.
  * Secondary School Marks: Minimum 60% in Class 10 (SSC) and Class 12 (Intermediate/CBSE).
  * Training Attendance: Minimum 90% attendance in all pre-placement skill development sessions (Aptitude, Coding, Soft Skills).
  * Punctuality: Failure to attend a registered campus recruitment test without prior medical leave will lead to debarment from the next 2 visiting companies.

STUDENT HANDBOOK: CAMPUS LIFE, CONDUCT AND POLICIES
====================================================

Section 1: Campus Decorum, Identification and Timings
1.1 College Hours and Identity Cards
The regular instructional hours of the college are from 8:30 AM to 4:45 PM, Monday through Friday. Every student must wear the official RFID Student Identity Card prominently around the neck at all times while inside the academic campus, laboratories, and library. Security staff are authorized to deny entry to any student without a valid ID card.

  * Central Library Hours: Open from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays; 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM on Saturdays.
  * Hostel Timings: Hostel gates close strictly at 9:00 PM for all resident students.
  * Vehicle Regulations: Students riding two-wheelers must wear helmets. Speed limit on campus is 20 km/h.

Section 2: Anti-Ragging Statutory Guidelines
2.1 Zero-Tolerance Anti-Ragging Mandate
Ragging in any form is strictly banned inside and outside the college campus as per UGC Regulations 2009 and Supreme Court of India directives. Ragging is defined as any disorderly conduct whether by words spoken or written, or by an act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness any student.
